# uptimekuma_proxy (Resource)

An outbound proxy that HTTP-based monitors can send their requests through.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimekuma_proxy" "egress" {
  protocol = "http"
  host     = "proxy.internal"
  port     = 3128
  username = "kuma"
  password = var.proxy_password
}

resource "uptimekuma_monitor_http" "external" {
  name     = "External API"
  url      = "https://api.partner.example.com/health"
  proxy_id = uptimekuma_proxy.egress.id
}

variable "proxy_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Proxy hostname or IP address.
- `port` (Number) Proxy port.
- `protocol` (String) Proxy protocol: `http`, `https`, `socks`, `socks4` or `socks5`.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the proxy can be used. Default: true.
- `apply_existing` (Boolean) When true, apply this proxy to every existing monitor at apply time. This is a one-shot server action, not stored state, so Terraform cannot detect drift in it.
- `default` (Boolean) Use this proxy by default for new monitors. Setting it deactivates the previous default. Default: false.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for proxy authentication.
- `username` (String) Username for proxy authentication. Setting this or `password` enables authentication.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric ID of the proxy, assigned by Uptime Kuma.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Monitors, tags, notifications and the rest are imported by their numeric ID,
# which is visible in the Uptime Kuma URL when you open the object.
terraform import uptimekuma_proxy.example 1
```
